questions.question: Article 32 of the Constitution of India deals with ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Right to Constitutional remedies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr B. R. Ambedkar.
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted to any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as the Right to Constitutional Remedies__.

 
 

 __Article__
 __Consists of__
 
 

 **Article 32**
 
 
Right to move the Supreme court for the enforcement of fundamental rights including the **writs**.

 __
 
• habeas corpus
 
• mandamus
 
• prohibition
 
• certiorari
 
• quo warranto
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Extra facts:

__
 
• Habeas Corpus: 

 
 
• This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained whether in prison or in private custody, before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
 
 
 
• Mandamus:
 
 
• The writ of command is issued by the supreme or high court when any government, court, corporation, or any public authority has to do a public duty but fails to do so.
 
 
 
• Prohibition:
 
 
• It is a writ issued with a view to restraining a person from holding a public office to which he is not entitled.
 
 
 
• Certiorari: 
 
 
• The writ of certiorari can be issued by the supreme or high court for quashing the order already passed by an inferior court, tribunal or quasi-judicial authority.
 
 
 
• Quo-Warranto: 
 
 
• The writ of quo-warranto can be issued by the supreme or high court for asking by what authority or warrant.
 
• It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Article 19 related to** Right to freedom.**
 
• The Right to freedom of speech and expression is a Fundamental Right under Article 19 of the Constitution of India.
 
• **There are six rights regarding freedom of:**
 
 
• Speech and expression
 
• Assembly
 
• Association
 
• Movement
 
• Residence
 
• Profession
 
 
 
• Article 25 of the Indian constitution guarantees the Right to Freedom of Religion to its citizens.
 
 
• It provides freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
 
• It is a basic human right guarantee that cannot be subverted or misinterpreted in any manner.
 
• Article 25 to Article 28 of the Indian constitution deals with the Right to Freedom of Religion.
 
 
 
• **The Right to Equality is mentioned in Articles 14 to18.**

questions.question: Who among the following gave the concept of ‘paradox of thrift’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __John Maynard Keynes__.

__
 
• **John Maynard Keynes gave the concept of the ‘paradox of thrift’.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

Paradox of Thrift :

__
 
• This concept talks about the ill effects of the personal savings of an individual on the economy.
 
• According to Keynes, During a recession in the economy, people tend to save more money as deposits rather than spending it.
 
• It leads to a decrease in aggregate demand and production falls, due to which the wages are reduced to counterbalance the fall in production.
 
• Hence the amounts of money available in the hands of people decrease and ultimately their savings also fall.
 
• In turn, the amount of money available to banks to lend as loans will decrease and the economy will go into a deeper recession.
 
• The concept is a paradox because according to it the savings of people will decrease because of the increase in their savings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to Adam Smith, the tax paid by an individual should not be arbitrary but it should be certain because the tax paid by an individual has no connection with the benefit received by him/her.
 
• In order to guide the taxing authority, Adam Smith laid down four principles which are also known as the Canons of taxation:
 
 
• Canon of Equality
 
• Canon of Certainty
 
• Canon of Convenience
 
• Canon of Economy
 
 
 
• Later, other economists also extended the list of Canons by Adam Smith:
 
 
• Canon of Productivity
 
• Canon of Elasticity
 
• Canon of Simplicity
 
• Canon of Variety
 
• Canon of Flexibility
 
 
 
• Amartya Sen:
 
 
• He is a famous economist and philosopher.
 
• He won the Bharat Ratna award in the year 1999.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998.

questions.question: 'Force’ divided by ‘mass’ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a**cceleration__.

__
 
• **'Force’ divided by ‘mass’ is equal to acceleration.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

Explanation: 

 
• Newton's second law is often stated as F = ma, which means the force (F) acting on an object is equal to the mass (m) of the object times its acceleration (a). This means the more mass an object has, the more force you need to accelerate it, and the greater the force, the greater the object's acceleration.

 
 
• Force(F) = Mass(m) × Acceleration(a).
 
 
 
• Unit of Force = SI unit of Force is in Newtons (N).
 
• 1 Newton is equal to 1 kg*m*s-2.
 
• The acceleration of an object is directly related to the net force and inversely related to its mass.
 
• The acceleration of an object depends on two things, force and mass.
 
• Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object.
 
• Mass is usually measured in grams (g) or kilograms (kg).
 
• An object's mass is constant in all circumstances, contrast this with its weight, a force that depends on gravity.

questions.question: Which of the following is dimensionless?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Longitudinal strain.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• The powers to which fundamental quantities must be raised in order to express the given physical quantity are called its dimensions.
 
• A quantity without dimension will usually be a ratio of two quantities with similar dimensions and, hence, cancel out.
 
• Thus, they will have no units.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• **Longitudinal stress:**

 
 
• Longitudinal stress is the stress which acts along the length and its unit is **N/m² or Pascal.**
 
 
 
• **Shear stress: **
 
 
• **​**If the deforming force acts tangentially to the surface of the body, It produces a change in the shape of the body.
 
• This tangential force applied per unit area is called shear stress.
 
• Its unit is ** N/mm2 or MPa. **
 
 
 
• **Deforming force: **
 
 
• **​**Deforming Force An external force applied to a body that changes its size or shape or both is called deforming force.
 
• its unit is** N or kg-m/s².**
 
 
 
• **Longitudinal strain: **
 
 
• **​**The change in the length (ΔL) to the original length (L) of the body is known as longitudinal strain.
 
 

i.e., Longitudinal strain = frac{{{{Delta }}L}}{L}

 
• And since it is a ratio of two lengths, hence it is a **dimensionless **quantity.

questions.question: How many oxygen atoms are there in a molecule of sodium peroxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Two**__**.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The structure of the molecule sodium peroxide is with** each sodium joined to one oxygen** and **the two oxygen joined with one bond to each other and the other bond to the sodium atoms.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/caedb1a2ae4216c71b81614744a4a5df26c0ff5e2c2b9bb070b706642bfa6c6f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Oxygen electronic configuration is ****1s²2s²2p⁴** .
 
• **Oxygen forms two bonds to fill the two half-filled p orbitals.**
 
• The one bond that is shared between the two Oxygen atoms does not affect the Oxidation state of Oxygen.
 
• The **two Oxygen atoms have equal electro negativity so there is no loss or gain of electrons in that bond.**
 
• The bond that Oxygen shares with Sodium do change the Oxidation state of both Sodium and Oxygen.
 
• **Sodium with a much lower electronegativity will give up one electron to the Oxygen becoming +-1 ( Sodium is oxidized) **
 
• **The Oxygen having a much high electronegativity will take an electron from the Sodium becoming (-1) The Oxygen is reduced.**
 
• **Lewis structure of Sodium Peroxide**:
 
 
• **..**
 
• **Na: O :**
 
• **..**
 
• **O: Na**
 
 
 
• This Lewis dot structure shows the "shared" electrons between the Sodium and Oxygen atoms.
 
• This results in the **transfer of an electron from the Sodium to the Oxygen resulting in the +1 charge for Sodium and the -1 charge for Oxygen.**
 
• The shared electrons between the two Oxygens result in no loss or gain of electrons.
